dimensions.assessment: Directly impacts the State of North Dakota, Indian Tribes with reservations in the state, holders of federal/state grazing permits, and users of public lands.
dimensions.evidence: authorizes the State to select in accordance with this Act 1 or more parcels of unappropriated Federal land of substantially equivalent value

dimensions.assessment: Substantially alters land ownership, mineral rights, and trust status for extensive parcels within Indian reservations and public lands in North Dakota.
dimensions.evidence: the portion of the State land grant parcel located within the boundaries of the reservation shall be... taken into trust by the Secretary on behalf of, and for the benefit of, the Indian Tribe

dimensions.assessment: Involves complex land valuations, appraisals, equalization payments, ledger accounts, and adjustments for mineral revenue sharing obligations.
dimensions.evidence: the party conveying the parcel of lesser value shall... equalize the value by the payment of funds... or enter the imbalance in value on a ledger account

dimensions.assessment: Enacts broad new authorities for land exchanges, appraisals, trust conveyances, and management exemptions from standard federal land laws.
dimensions.evidence: conveyance of unappropriated Federal land by the Secretary under this Act... shall not be considered a sale, exchange, or conveyance for purposes of section 203, 205, 206, or 209 of FLPMA

dimensions.assessment: Permanently transfers titles, establishes trust lands, and sets up multi-year ledger reconciliation processes.
dimensions.evidence: each ledger account... shall be balanced not later than 3 years... and closed not later than 5 years after the date of the last conveyance

summary: The North Dakota Trust Lands Completion Act of 2026 allows the State of North Dakota to exchange state land grant parcels located within Indian reservations for unappropriated federal land managed by the Bureau of Land Management of substantially equivalent value. Upon the request of an affected Indian tribe, the Secretary of the Interior must place the exchanged state land located within that tribe's reservation into trust for the tribe's benefit. The bill also establishes rules for land valuation, appraisals, ledger accounts, environmental and hazardous materials certifications, and the continuation of existing grazing operations.

affected_groups.effect: Can exchange certain state land grant parcels located within Indian reservations for unappropriated federal land of equivalent value, and must convey title free of financial encumbrances.
affected_groups.group: State of North Dakota (Board of University and School Lands and Department of Trust Lands)

affected_groups.effect: Can request that the Secretary of the Interior hold relinquished state land located within their reservation in trust on their behalf, making that land part of their reservation.
Allowed to continue active domestic livestock grazing operations on exchanged land for the remainder of their lease, permit, or contract term under existing terms and conditions.
Must review, approve or reject state land selections, conduct appraisals, complete hazardous materials inspections, and convey unappropriated federal land to the state.
affected_groups.group: Federal Government (Department of the Interior and Bureau of Land Management)

key_provisions: Authorizes the State of North Dakota to relinquish state land grant parcels located wholly or partially within Indian reservations in exchange for unappropriated federal land of substantially equivalent value.
Requires the Secretary of the Interior, at the request of an Indian tribe, to take relinquished state land located within that tribe's reservation into trust for the benefit of the tribe.

Mandates that the overall value of land parcels in an exchange be substantially equal, allowing for equalization payments or ledger accounts for imbalances up to 25 percent of the federal land's total value.
Requires independent appraisals (or mass/summary appraisals for low-value parcels under $500,000 and $500 per acre) and public notice of final appraisals.
Requires both the Secretary and the State to complete inspections and hazardous materials certifications prior to completing conveyances.
Provides for the continuation of active domestic livestock grazing operations on land exchanged under the bill for the remainder of the existing lease, permit, or contract term.
missing_information: The total acreage, exact number of parcels, or specific economic value of the lands eligible for exchange are not specified in the text.
The names of the specific Indian tribes that will request land to be held in trust are not listed.
summary_detail.plain_summary: The North Dakota Trust Lands Completion Act of 2026 allows the State of North Dakota to exchange state land grant parcels located within Indian reservations for unappropriated federal land managed by the Bureau of Land Management of substantially equivalent value. Upon the request of an affected Indian tribe, the Secretary of the Interior must place the exchanged state land located within that tribe's reservation into trust for the tribe's benefit. The bill also establishes rules for land valuation, appraisals, ledger accounts, environmental and hazardous materials certifications, and the continuation of existing grazing operations.
summary_detail.significance: This legislation alters land ownership patterns between the State of North Dakota, the federal government, and tribal nations by consolidating state-owned revenue-generating lands outside of reservations and returning reservation lands to tribal trusts.
